newsitem.title: UK: UK air traffic union tries to defuse sell-off row.
newsitem.headline: UK air traffic union tries to defuse sell-off row.

text.p: The union representing Britain's air traffic controllers on Thursday tried to defuse a row over whether a future Labour government would privatise the National Air Traffic Services.

The ruling Conservatives have accused Labour of changing its mind over the sell-off, pointing to a letter by Joe Magee of the Institute of Professionals, Managers and Specialists (IPMS), who said he had been assured by the opposition party's transport department in March that NATS would not be sold off.

In recent days Labour officials have consistently said the party has not yet decided whether NATS should be sold off. They suggested Magee had merely spoken to someone in the office of the party's transport department rather than a policy-maker.
With Labour under fire over an apparent U-turn on the issue, the IPMS issued a statement backing the party's line and making no mention of Magee's letter.

"IPMS sought the assurance from the Labour party in the middle of March. A member of staff in the shadow transport team's office explained that no decision had been taken and no such assurance (that the privatisation planned would be scrapped) could be given," the statement said.

Union general secretary Bill Brett said in the statement: "IPMS has already made a strong case against privatising NATS on safety grounds and have won considerable public support for its arguments. We were told that the matter would be reviewed when Labour was in government."
Labour finance spokesman Alistair Darling told BBC radio earlier on Thursday that the poor state of Britain's public finances meant the party might have to consider privatising NATS to raise funds.
Labour is comfortably ahead in opinion polls and is widely expected to win the May 1 general election.
